result.title: How Much Computation Does Every Forecast Need? Structured Block Skipping in Two Time-Series Foundation Models
result.summary: Time-series foundation models use the same network depth for every input, although forecasting windows differ in structure and difficulty. We test whether whole Transformer blocks can be removed at inference time in two pretrained models: Chronos-Bolt and TimesFM 2.5. Our bypasses avoid the original block computation and preserve the dense model exactly when all blocks are enabled. Masks are selected only on calibration windows and evaluated on 1,088 held-out windows from ETTh1, Traffic, Weather, and Exchange. At moderate sparsity, Chronos-Bolt with 7/11 candidate blocks and TimesFM with 16/20 blocks show little change in mean relative forecasting quality across datasets while reducing median A100 batch-1 latency by 11.2% and 13.4%. More aggressive TimesFM skipping accelerates inference further but substantially harms Traffic and Weather. Across both models, different equal-budget masks win on different windows, and a retrospective oracle significantly improves over the best static mask on every dataset. However, dataset-specific masks transfer inconsistently, and Chronos representations do not support reliable unseen-domain routing. These results establish cross-architecture structured redundancy and input-dependent opportunity, but not a deployable dynamic inference method.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在 Chronos-Bolt 与 TimesFM 2.5 两个时间序列基础模型上，测试推理期整体跳过 Transformer block 的可行性：用校准集选掩码、在留出窗口上评估，发现中等稀疏度下精度几乎不变但延迟下降，且不同输入各有权重不同的最优掩码。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按输入分配计算量」的掩码选择、全开时严格等价于稠密模型的门控设计，以及 oracle 上界与静态掩码差距、路由泛化失败的诊断，可供核查 LVR 中 THINK/LOOK/STOP 预算分配与停止决策的收益—成本评估，但跨领域迁移仅为可能线索。
